segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: Hello, South City Cycling Club.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Oh, hi. Er ... I want to find out about joining the club.

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: Right. I can help you there. I’m the club secretary and my name’s Jim Hunter .

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Oh, hi Jim.

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: So, are you interested in membership for yourself?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: That’s right.

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: OK. Well there are basically two types of adult membership. If you’re pretty serious about cycling, there’s the Full membership. That costs 260 dollars and that covers you not just for ordinary cycling but also for races both here in the city and also in other parts of Australia.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Right. Well, I’m not really up to that standard. I was more interested in just joining a group to do some cycling in my free time.

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: Sure. That’s why most people join. So, in that case you’d be better with the Recreational membership. That’s 108 dollars if you’re over 19, and 95 dollars if you’re under.

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: OK. It’s paid quarterly, and you can upgrade it later to the Full membership if you want to, of course. Now both types of membership include the club fee of 20 dollars. They also provide insurance in case you have an accident, though we hope you won’t need that, of course.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: No. OK, well, I’ll go with the Recreational membership, I think. And that allows me to join in the club activities, and so on?

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: That’s right. And once you’re a member of the club, you’re also permitted to wear our kit when you’re out cycling. It’s green and white.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes, I’ve seen cyclists wearing it. So, can I buy that at the club?

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: No, it’s made to order by a company in Brisbane. You can find them online: they’re called Jerriz. That’s J-E-R-R-I-Z. You can use your membership number to put in an order on their website.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: OK. Now, can you tell me a bit about the rides I can do?

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: Sure. So we have training rides pretty well every morning, and they’re a really good way of improving your cycling skills as well as your general level of fitness, but they’re different levels. Level A is pretty fast – you’re looking at about 30 or 35 kilometres an hour. If you can do about 25 kilometres an hour, you’d probably be level B, and then level C are the novices, who stay at about 15 kilometres per hour.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Right. Well I reckon I’d be level B. So, when are the sessions for that level?

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: There are a couple each week. They’re both early morning sessions. There’s one on Tuesdays, and for that one you meet at 5.30 am, and the meeting point’s the stadium – do you know where that is?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes, it’s quite near my home, in fact. OK, and how about the other one?

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: That’s on Thursdays. It starts at the same time, but they meet at the main gate to the park.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Is that the one just past the shopping mall?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: So how long are the rides?

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: They’re about an hour and a half. So, if you have a job it’s easy to fit in before you go to work. And the members often go somewhere for coffee afterwards, so it’s quite a social event.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: OK. That sounds good. I’ve only just moved to the city so I don’t actually know many people yet.

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: Well, it’s a great way to meet people.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: And does each ride have a leader?

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: Sometimes, but not always. But you don’t really need one; the group members on the ride support one another, anyway.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: How would we know where to go?

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: If you check the club website, you’ll see that the route for each ride is clearly marked. So you can just print that out and take it along with you. It’s similar from one week to another, but it’s not always exactly the same.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: And what do I need to bring?

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: Well, bring a bottle of water, and your phone. You shouldn’t use if while you’re cycling, buy have it with you.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Right.

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: And in winter, it’s well before sunrise when we set out, so you need to make sure your bike’s got lights.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: That’s OK. Well, thanks Jim. I’d definitely like to join. So what’s the best way of going about it?

segments.speaker: JIM
segments.en: You can ...

Questions 1-10
SOUTH CITY CYCLING CLUB
Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

      Example
      Name of club secretary: Jim .....Hunter.....
      Membership

      ● Recreational membership costs $108
      ● Cost of membership includes the club fee and [2] __________
      ● The club kit is made by a company called [3] __________
      Training rides
      ● Chance to improve cycling skills and fitness
      ● Level B: speed about [4] __________
      ● Weekly sessions:
      – Tuesdays at 5.30 am, meet at the [5] __________
      – Thursdays at 5.30 am, meet at the entrance to the [6] __________
      Further information
      ● Rides are about an hour and a half
      ● Members often have [7] __________ together afterwards
      ● There is not always a [8] __________ with the group on these rides
      ● Check and print the [9] __________ on the website beforehand
      ● Bikes must have [10] __________
Table Headers:
    South City Cycling Club
